blocks.text: Intellectual property concerns legally recognised rights in certain creations, inventions, brands and designs. A general idea is not automatically protected in every form. Rights can support licensing, differentiation and returns on investment.

bme-y11-u2-intellectual-property.title: Matching the right to the asset

blocks.text: Copyright generally protects original expression and arises automatically in Australia when qualifying material is recorded; there is no general Australian copyright registration system.

A patent protects a qualifying invention. A trade mark distinguishes goods or services. A design right concerns the appearance of a qualifying product. Trade secrets depend on maintaining confidentiality. A single product can involve several rights.

For a registrable right, identify the appropriate protection, search relevant existing rights, prepare the application, lodge with IP Australia and respond to examination or other requirements. Exact procedures differ between patents, trade marks and designs.

Design registration and certification are distinct stages; certification is required before enforcing a registered design. Registration does not mean IP Australia automatically prosecutes every infringement. Owners may need to pursue appropriate enforcement or licensing options.

Characterised by:
High R&D investment, because the product and technology is new and all the flaws need to be tested and fixed before it is ready for mass marketing
Low Sales, because consumers are either not aware of the product’s existence, are still using an alternative product or they don’t trust the new product yet.
High Expenses, because the product is incurring costs (e.g. R&D and marketing) but sales are low.
Low Profit (likely loss)
High promotion focus, because product awareness is critical to success.
Early Adopters are important because they support the early development of the product and introduce new products to the market
Example: VR headsets

Characterised by:
Increasing Sales, because consumers are becoming aware of the product’s existence and are switching from alternative products
Decreasing Expenses, because R&D needs have slowed down and the market is becoming more aware of the product’s existence.
Increasing Profits
Increased Competition, because of the products success, competing brands and products enter the market to enjoy the success that the original businesses are enjoying.
Consumer Loyalty Programs, because of the increased competition, consumer loyalty programs are useful to strengthen customer relationships.
Example: Smartphones

Characterised by:
Stabalising Sales, because many consumers are now aware of the product’s existence and those that want the product likely already have it
Stabalising Expenses, because marketing requirement are declining and production efficiency has increased.
Stable Profits
Few new customers, because customers who wanted the product already have it, and many product owners are looking to newer products
Differentiation focus, because businesses can continue to experience some success by differentiating their existing product e.g. Blueray, bluetooth connectivity
Example: DVD players

Characterised by:
Declining Sales, because many consumers now see the product as ‘old’ or have replaced it with other, newer products
Increasing Expenses, because production expenses climb as inputs become outdated.
Declining Profits
Product become obsolete, because customers see no use for this product, especially when there are newer and cheaper products available
Exit strategies planned, businesses must decide how they will exit the market and stop producing the product e.g. what technical assistance may they still offer? When will they stop producing? What will they do with any leftover inventory? What will they produce instead?
Example: VHS Tapes

bme-y11-u2-marketing-across-the-product-.title: Marketing Strategy for Different Phases of PLC

blocks.text:
Clever marketers know that during different phases of the Product Lifecycle, success is possible with deliberate and distinct marketing activities.
Marketers must first be able to determine which phase of the PLC the product is in, and then take steps to maximise sales, brand loyalty and other measures of success within that phase.
They must also be aware of when one phase is coming to an end, to change tactics and successfully enter the next phase.

The primary purpose of a business plan is to outline the company's goals, strategies, and operational details to guide its development, growth and success.
This plan outlines the key decisions that will guide the direction of the business.
What key decisions help to achieve success?

The business plan provides direction and clarity to both internal stakeholders (e.g. owners) and external stakeholders (such as investors, lenders, and partners).
The key purposes include:
setting clear objectives
securing financing and attracting investors
aligning team members
clarifying the mission and vision

The intent of the business plan is tailored to the specific needs and goals of the business.
Whether it's securing funding, guiding expansion, or managing a leadership transition, the business plan plays a crucial role in helping the business achieve its objectives.
Why are we writing this Business Plan?

bme-y11-u2-business-planning.title: Intent Example: Start-Up Seeking Investor Funding

blocks.text:
The primary intent of the business plan for this scenario is to attract potential investors and secure funding for the startup.
The plan serves as a persuasive tool to demonstrate the viability of the business concept, the growth potential, and the profitability to potential investors.
It provides a clear roadmap for how the invested capital will be used to achieve specific milestones and generate returns for investors.

In this scenario, the intent of the business plan is to outline the strategic steps required for the established business to successfully expand into a new market or launch a new product or service.
The plan helps the business assess the risks, opportunities, and potential challenges associated with the expansion. It also serves as a communication tool to align internal teams and secure any necessary additional resources or financing for the expansion.

For a family-owned business facing a leadership transition, the intent of the business plan is to ensure a smooth and successful transition of ownership and management to the next generation or new leadership. The plan outlines the succession process, including leadership training, ownership transfer, and long-term business sustainability strategies. It helps maintain continuity and protect the business's legacy while addressing potential conflicts or challenges within the family.

bme-y11-u2-business-planning.title: Purpose vs Intent - What’s the difference?

blocks.text:
The purpose of a business plan is to illustrate the overarching reason the business exists, and how it plans to achieve its overarching mission.
The intent of a business plan is the specific goal or outcome a business hopes to achieve by producing the plan, based on the overall direction of the business at that specific time e.g. start-up, expansion, diversification etc.

concise and compelling overview of the plan
a snapshot of the key points and critical aspects of the proposal
overview of the current position
overview of the future expected position of the business

the executive summary serves as a powerful tool for making a strong first impression and convincing stakeholders of the business' merit, making it a crucial component of any well-crafted business plan.

Key features of an executive summary include:
Summarise the business concept, its goals, target market, products or services, and the problem it aims to solve.
Highlight Key Points like market opportunities, competitive advantage, current and future positions, financial projections.
Clarify business objectives, helping the reader understand what the business seeks to achieve

The business concept is a concise description of the fundamental purpose, products or services, target market, and value proposition of a business.
This concept underpins the entire business plan and helps stakeholders understand what the business aims to achieve and how it plans to do so.

Netflix provides customers with monthly subscription-based, on-demand access to their entertainment on any device, anywhere, using its digital platform of licensed TV shows, movies and podcasts.

The primary purpose of a financial plan is to provide readers with estimates about the business’ future earnings (budgeted forecasts).
A financial plan is a critical component of a business plan, and its purpose is to provide a comprehensive overview of the financial forecast of the business.

Key features of a financial plan include:
Sales and Purchases forecast
Budgeted Profit and Loss Statement
Budgeted Monthly Cash Flow Statement
Break-Even Analysis

Sales and Purchases forecast layout the predicted amount of sales and the purchase is required for the upcoming year of the business.
Market research will be required to produce accurate forecasts and the business needs to take him to account normal fluctuations and trends.

A Budgeted Profit and Loss Statement will layout the predicted profit that will be generated by the business, based on its forecasted earnings.
The Profit and loss Statement will include an overview of predicted income and expenses.

A Budgeted Monthly Cash Flow Statement will also be produced to predict the future cash flow of the business. Cash flow is the amount of cash entering and leaving a business. This is different from profit as it simply indicates the flow of cash through a business, not whether it will ultimately turn into profit.
Cash flow can be measured by any/all of the five financial elements: assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses.
